test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The API answered with 423 Locked, a valid documented response meaning the account is locked after repeated failed logins — the endpoint itself works, so this is not an app bug. The test posts `password: 'pass123'`, which is not the demo app's standard customer password; wrong credentials repeatedly submitted are what lock the account, and the lock persists, which matches failure on all 3 attempts (ruling out flakiness). A lesser alternative is that another test locked the shared account, but the non-standard test credential is the more direct cause.
triage.evidence: "Expected: 200  Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);`, with request data `{ email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' }`; "Status: failed on every attempt (3 attempts)"
triage.next_step: Call POST /users/login manually (e.g. curl/Postman) with the documented demo password `welcome01` for a fresh customer account; if it returns 200, fix the credentials in tests/api.spec.ts line 5 and use a dedicated, non-shared account for the @smoke login test.

triage.reason: The intended empty-list mock never took effect: the route pattern `**/products` does not match the app's real products request, which carries a query string (page/filter params), and Playwright glob matching includes the query string. Consequently the real API response was rendered, and the page legitimately shows nine products with pagination — so the "no products" message is correctly absent. The locator failure is caused by faulty test setup, not by the app. Identical failure on all 3 attempts excludes flakiness.
triage.evidence: Test code: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` versus the rendered page: `link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"` and `navigation "Pagination": ... "You're on page 1", "page 2", "page 3"`. Error: `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed ... Locator: getByText('There are no products found.') ... element(s) not found`.
triage.next_step: Broaden the mock to match the real request URL — e.g. `await page.route('**/products**', ...)` (or `/\/products(\?.*)?$/`) — then re-run and confirm via a `page.on('request')` log or trace that the products call was fulfilled with the empty payload.

The element the test needs exists but the app renders it without its label/aria-label, so the role+name query cannot match. This is reinforced by a cluster of identical label defects elsewhere on the same page ("Sorth" instead of "Sort", "Contakt" instead of "Contact", and a "Home" link pointing at #/contact), consistent with the banner "Bug Hunting Mode - Find & Report Bugs!". A role-based locator on a labelled search field is a reasonable check; the app failed to expose the label. Some chance this is instead a deliberate UI rename the test never tracked (broken script), but the missing name plus the misspelling pattern favours an app defect.
triage.evidence: Error: "locator.fill: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Search' })" vs. the page snapshot: "- heading \"Search\" [level=4] [ref=e54] ... - textbox [ref=e59] - button \"X\" [ref=e60] - button \"Serch\" [ref=e61]"
triage.next_step: Open the search widget in the app's DOM (devtools) and check the input element for a missing/removed aria-label, placeholder or associated <label for>, and the button text "Serch"; file a UI-label defect if the markup lost its accessible name, then re-run the test once the label is restored.

What never happened is a response matching the test's predicate, which demands an exotic HTTP method and an exact URL tail: `response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')`. Toolshop fetches filtered products with a GET to `/products?by_category=...` (query string, so it also doesn't end with `/products`), so `page.waitForResponse` can never resolve and burns the 30s budget on all 3 attempts. Deterministic failure on every attempt also argues against flakiness, and the filtering feature itself demonstrably works in the captured page state.
triage.evidence: Predicate: `response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')` vs. page state after the click: `checkbox "Pliers" [checked] [active]` with results `link "ECO Combination Pliers ... $14.15"`, `link "ECO Pliers ... $12.01"` — error: `page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.`
